detail: The non-synchronous census initiated large-scale demographic classification and data collection across much of the subcontinent.
Vallabhbhai Patel, the independence leader and statesman central to the political integration of princely states, was born.
The reform movement promoted Vedic revival, education, social reform and a new form of organised Hindu public life.

text: The Bombay Stock Exchange is established
detail: Asia’s oldest stock exchange created a formal market for securities and became a central institution of Indian finance.

text: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College is founded at Aligarh
detail: The institution became a centre of modern education for Indian Muslims and later developed into Aligarh Muslim University.

text: The Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science is founded
detail: The institution became the first major national organisation devoted to scientific research and public science education in India.
Muhammad Iqbal, the Urdu and Persian poet-philosopher whose work profoundly shaped Muslim intellectual and political culture in South Asia, was born.

text: The Vernacular Press Act restricts Indian-language newspapers
detail: The law targeted critical vernacular publications and became a defining episode in the struggle for press freedom.
Periyar E. V. Ramasamy, the social reformer associated with the Self-Respect Movement and anti-caste politics in Tamil Nadu, was born.
Sarojini Naidu, the poet, nationalist and women’s-rights leader, was born.
Munshi Premchand, the Hindi-Urdu novelist and short-story writer who transformed modern social realism, was born.

text: The first Indian Factory Act is enacted
detail: The law introduced limited regulation of child labour and working hours in factories, marking the beginnings of industrial labour legislation.

text: The first synchronous census of India is conducted
detail: The census established decennial population enumeration and generated extensive statistical records used by administrators, scholars and later planners.

text: Bankim Chandra's Anandamath is published, carrying Vande Mataram
detail: The novel's hymn to the motherland becomes the anthem of the freedom movement and, in 1950, India's national song.

text: Telephone exchanges open in Calcutta, Bombay and Madras
detail: Commercial telephone service began in the three presidency cities, creating a new form of instantaneous urban communication.
Rajendra Prasad, first President of India (1950–1962), was born.

text: The Indian National Congress is founded
detail: The organisation created an all-India political forum and became the principal institutional vehicle of the independence movement.
Srinivasa Ramanujan, the mathematician whose work transformed number theory, infinite series and mathematical analysis, was born.
Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, the philosopher and educator who interpreted Indian philosophy for global audiences, was born.
Jawaharlal Nehru, the independence leader and first prime minister of India, associated with parliamentary institutions and scientific planning, was born.
Jyotirao Phule, the anti-caste reformer and pioneer of education for women and marginalised communities, died.
B. R. Ambedkar, the jurist, economist and social reformer who chaired the Constitution’s drafting committee, was born.
Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, the educator, Sanskrit scholar and social reformer associated with widow remarriage and Bengali prose, died.

text: Dadabhai Naoroji is elected to the British Parliament
detail: The 'Grand Old Man of India' wins Finsbury Central by five votes — the first Indian MP at Westminster — and uses the seat to argue his 'drain of wealth' theory.

text: Swami Vivekananda addresses the Parliament of Religions
detail: His Chicago speeches brought Vedanta and yoga to a wide international audience and reshaped global perceptions of Indian religious thought.
Satyendra Nath Bose, the physicist whose work on quantum statistics led to the concept of bosons, was born.
V. V. Giri, President of India (1969–1974), was born.

text: Jagadish Chandra Bose demonstrates wireless signalling
detail: Bose’s experiments in Calcutta demonstrated the generation and detection of millimetre waves and contributed to early radio science.

Morarji Desai, Prime Minister of India (1977–1979), was born.

text: Cinema is publicly exhibited in India
detail: The Lumière films screened at Bombay’s Watson’s Hotel introduced moving pictures to Indian audiences and helped launch a new mass medium.
The epidemic caused large-scale mortality, migration and coercive public-health measures, profoundly affecting urban governance and medical policy.
Subhas Chandra Bose, the nationalist leader who sought Indian independence through international alliances and armed organisation, was born.

Savitribai Phule, the pioneering teacher, poet and campaigner for women’s and anti-caste education, died.

text: The Sidrapong hydroelectric station begins operation
detail: The plant near Darjeeling became India’s first commercial hydroelectric power station.
Gulzarilal Nanda, twice acting Prime Minister of India, was born.

text: Norman Pritchard wins India's first Olympic medals
detail: Representing India at the Paris Games, Pritchard takes silver in the 200 m and 200 m hurdles — the first Olympic medals credited to an Asian nation.
Charan Singh, Prime Minister of India (1979–1980), was born.
Swami Vivekananda, the monk and global interpreter of Vedanta who founded the Ramakrishna Mission, died.

text: Electric trams begin operating in Calcutta
detail: The electrification of the tramway created one of Asia’s early large urban electric transit systems.

text: Gauhar Jaan makes landmark gramophone recordings
detail: Her Calcutta recordings were among the earliest commercially successful Indian music discs and helped create a modern recorded-music industry.
Lal Bahadur Shastri, the independence activist and prime minister associated with food self-reliance and the slogan Jai Jawan Jai Kisan, was born.
Rukmini Devi Arundale, the dancer and institution-builder who helped reshape the modern presentation of Bharatanatyam, was born.
Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, President of India (1974–1977), died in office, was born.
Mohammad Hidayatullah, acting President of India (1969) and Chief Justice, was born.

text: The Swadeshi movement accelerates indigenous enterprise and education
detail: The movement promoted domestic industry, national education, public associations and cultural production in response to the partition of Bengal.

text: The Cellular Jail is completed at Port Blair
detail: The Andamans' 'Kala Pani' becomes the dreaded prison of the freedom struggle; Savarkar is among its most famous inmates.
Bhagat Singh, the revolutionary thinker whose execution made him an enduring symbol of anti-colonial sacrifice, was born.

text: Tata Iron and Steel Company is founded
detail: The company created the foundation for large-scale integrated steel production in India and the industrial city of Jamshedpur.

text: Khudiram Bose is executed at eighteen
detail: One of the youngest revolutionaries of the freedom struggle, hanged for the Muzaffarpur bombing; his death stirs Bengal.
Homi J. Bhabha, the physicist and institution-builder regarded as the architect of India’s nuclear programme, was born.

text: The Indian Institute of Science begins academic work
detail: The Bengaluru institution became one of India’s premier centres for advanced research in science and engineering.
R. Venkataraman, President of India (1987–1992), was born.
Faiz Ahmed Faiz, the Urdu poet whose work joined lyricism, social justice and anti-colonial politics, was born.

text: India’s first official airmail flight takes place
detail: A flight from Allahabad to Naini carried mail across the Yamuna and became a landmark in global aviation and postal history.

text: Jana Gana Mana is sung for the first time
detail: Tagore's hymn is first performed at the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress on 27 December 1911; it becomes the national anthem in 1950.

text: Mohun Bagan win the IFA Shield barefoot
detail: The Calcutta club defeats the East Yorkshire Regiment 2–1 — the first Indian side to win the Shield, celebrated across the country as a nationalist triumph.

text: The imperial capital is shifted from Calcutta to Delhi
detail: The decision initiated the planning and construction of New Delhi and reoriented the administrative geography of British India.
B. D. Jatti, acting President of India (1977), was born.
Amrita Sher-Gil, the painter who became a foundational figure in modern Indian art, was born.
Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, President of India (1977–1982), was born.

text: Rabindranath Tagore receives the Nobel Prize in Literature
detail: Tagore became the first Asian Nobel laureate, bringing modern Indian literature to unprecedented global attention.

text: Raja Harishchandra inaugurates Indian feature filmmaking
detail: Dadasaheb Phalke’s silent film is widely regarded as the first full-length Indian feature film.
Gopal Krishna Gokhale, the liberal nationalist, economist and founder of the Servants of India Society, died.
Bismillah Khan, the shehnai maestro who brought the instrument to the centre of Indian classical concert culture, was born.

M. S. Subbulakshmi, the Carnatic vocalist who became one of India’s most celebrated classical musicians, was born.

text: The Lucknow Pact unites Congress and the Muslim League

text: Champaran: Gandhi's first satyagraha in India
detail: Taking up the cause of indigo cultivators in north Bihar, Gandhi tests in India the method he forged in South Africa — and wins.

Shankar Dayal Sharma, President of India (1992–1997), was born.

Vikram Sarabhai, the physicist and institution-builder regarded as the father of India’s space programme, was born.

text: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre transforms Indian public opinion
detail: The killing of unarmed civilians in Amritsar became a decisive moral rupture in the relationship between colonial rule and the Indian public.

text: The Rowlatt Act extends wartime repression
detail: Detention without trial in peacetime provokes nationwide hartals — the road that leads to Jallianwala Bagh.
K. R. Narayanan, President of India (1997–2002), was born.
Ravi Shankar, the sitarist and composer who became a global ambassador of Hindustani classical music, was born.
Bal Gangadhar Tilak, the nationalist leader, journalist and public organiser, died.

Subramania Bharati, the Tamil poet and journalist whose modernist and nationalist verse reshaped Tamil literature, died.

text: The Gateway of India is completed at Bombay
detail: Built to commemorate George V's 1911 visit; twenty-four years later the last British troops leave India through the same arch.

text: India wins its first Olympic hockey gold medal
detail: The Amsterdam victory began an era of dominance in field hockey and made sport a prominent part of modern Indian public culture.

detail: The law established minimum marriage ages and marked a major, though limited, intervention in social custom and child welfare.

detail: Three conferences on India's constitutional future; only the second, with Gandhi as Congress's sole delegate, carries real drama.

Bhagat Singh, the revolutionary thinker whose execution made him an enduring symbol of anti-colonial sacrifice, died.

text: Alam Ara inaugurates Indian sound cinema
detail: The first Indian talkie transformed film production, acting and music and established songs as a defining feature of South Asian cinema.

detail: The court became the subcontinent’s highest federal judicial body and a direct institutional predecessor of the Supreme Court of India.

text: The Bengal famine causes catastrophic mortality
detail: Wartime disruption, inflation, policy failure and food-market collapse produced one of the deadliest famines of the twentieth century.

text: The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research is founded
detail: TIFR became a central institution for Indian research in physics, mathematics, computing and later space and nuclear science.

text: Partition triggers one of the largest forced migrations in history
detail: The drawing of new borders displaced millions and produced enduring demographic, cultural and political consequences across India and Pakistan.

text: The princely states are integrated into India
detail: Sardar Patel and V.P. Menon bring 560-odd princely states into the Union by persuasion, pressure and accession — the map of modern India takes shape.
Mahatma Gandhi, the leader and thinker who developed mass non-violent resistance and became central to India’s independence movement, died.

text: Free India's first Olympic hockey gold
detail: At the London Games, independent India's hockey team beats Great Britain 4–0 in the final — a fourth straight gold, and the first under its own flag.

text: The Reserve Bank of India is nationalised

text: The first Asian Games are held in New Delhi
detail: The multi-sport event helped institutionalise Asian sporting cooperation and established India as an early host of major international games.

text: India completes its first general election
detail: Hundreds of millions of citizens participated in the world’s largest experiment in universal adult franchise.

text: AIIMS is established in New Delhi
detail: The institute combined advanced medical education, research and tertiary care and became a model for public medical institutions.

detail: The Trombay reactor marked a major step in India’s indigenous nuclear-science and isotope-production capability.

text: The Defence Research and Development Organisation is formed
detail: DRDO consolidated defence laboratories and became a principal institution for aerospace, electronics, missiles, materials and military research.

text: Experimental television broadcasting begins in Delhi
detail: The launch of television service by All India Radio began the development of Doordarshan and a new national mass medium.

text: Bombay State is divided into Maharashtra and Gujarat
detail: The linguistic reorganisation created two major states and reshaped the political and economic geography of western India.

text: The Indus Waters Treaty is signed
detail: India and Pakistan agreed on the allocation and management of the Indus river system, creating one of the world’s most durable transboundary water frameworks.

text: Bhakra Dam is dedicated to the nation
detail: The dam and irrigation-power complex became one of the emblematic infrastructure projects of post-independence India.

detail: The launch from the equatorial rocket station began India’s operational space programme and atmospheric-science research.

Shah Rukh Khan, the actor whose global popularity made him one of the most influential figures in modern Hindi cinema, was born.

text: The Food Corporation of India is established
detail: FCI became the central agency for grain procurement, storage and distribution, supporting food security and the public distribution system.

text: The National Dairy Development Board is created

Lal Bahadur Shastri, the prime minister associated with food self-reliance and the slogan Jai Jawan Jai Kisan, died.

detail: New seed varieties, irrigation, fertiliser and procurement policies launched the Green Revolution and reduced chronic dependence on grain imports.

detail: Hours after signing the peace with Pakistan that closed the 1965 war, Prime Minister Shastri dies in Tashkent.

detail: The reform expanded state control over credit and accelerated branch banking in rural and underserved regions.

detail: ISRO created a national programme for satellites, launch vehicles, remote sensing, communications and space science.

text: The Chipko movement gains national attention

detail: The underground test demonstrated nuclear-explosive capability and permanently altered India’s scientific and strategic position.

detail: The law created a statutory framework for autonomous public broadcasting through Doordarshan and All India Radio.
Amid insurgency and targeted killings, most of the Valley's Pandit community leaves in the early months of 1990 — an exodus of well over a hundred thousand people.

text: The Mandal Commission recommendations are implemented
detail: The extension of reservations to Other Backward Classes transformed access to public employment, party politics and debates on social justice.
Rajiv Gandhi, the prime minister associated with telecommunications, computerisation and administrative modernisation, died.
Industrial licensing was dismantled, trade and investment rules were loosened and the economy moved toward greater competition and global integration.
C-DAC’s machine demonstrated that India could develop high-performance computing despite technology-denial restrictions.
Mohammad Hidayatullah, acting President of India (1969) and Chief Justice, died.
Satyajit Ray, the filmmaker, writer and designer whose work transformed Indian and world cinema, died.

text: The Babri Masjid is demolished at Ayodhya
detail: Kar sevaks tear down the sixteenth-century mosque on 6 December; the demolition and the riots that follow mark a turning point in the politics of religion in India.

text: The Seventy-third and Seventy-fourth Amendments strengthen local government
detail: The amendments gave constitutional status to panchayats and municipalities and mandated regular elections and representation for women and marginalised communities.
J. R. D. Tata, the industrialist and institution-builder who shaped Indian aviation, industry and philanthropy, died.
Thirteen coordinated bombings on 12 March kill 257 people — retaliation, the plotters said, for the riots that followed Ayodhya.

text: The National Stock Exchange is incorporated
detail: The exchange introduced nationwide electronic trading and helped modernise Indian capital markets, transparency and settlement systems.
Giani Zail Singh, President of India (1982–1987), died.
Morarji Desai, Prime Minister of India (1977–1979), died.

text: India’s first commercial mobile-phone call is made
detail: The call between Kolkata and New Delhi marked the beginning of cellular telephony and the later mass mobile revolution.

text: Public internet service begins in India
detail: VSNL’s commercial internet launch connected Indian users to the global internet and initiated a transformation in communication, business and media.
Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, President of India (1977–1982), died.
Mother Teresa, the Catholic nun and founder of the Missionaries of Charity, associated with service to the poor and sick, died.
The railway linked the western coast through difficult mountain and river terrain using hundreds of bridges and tunnels.
Gulzarilal Nanda, twice acting Prime Minister of India, died.

text: India conducts the Pokhran-II nuclear tests
detail: The series of underground tests declared India’s nuclear-weapons capability and altered its international strategic and technological position.
Shankar Dayal Sharma, President of India (1992–1997), died.

text: The New Telecom Policy accelerates competition and mobile growth
detail: The policy shifted licensing toward revenue sharing and helped create the conditions for rapid expansion of affordable telecommunications.

text: Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand are created
detail: The formation of three new states altered India’s federal map and responded to long-running regional demands.

text: The Information Technology Act is enacted
detail: India’s first comprehensive cyber-law framework recognised electronic records and signatures and regulated offences in digital networks.
R. K. Narayan, the novelist whose Malgudi stories became classics of Indian English literature, died.

text: The Golden Quadrilateral highway programme begins
detail: The national highway project connected Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata and transformed long-distance road freight and travel.
The earthquake killed thousands, destroyed towns and prompted major changes in disaster management, building codes and reconstruction policy.
Five gunmen strike Parliament House on 13 December; the attack brings India and Pakistan to the brink of war through 2002.
B. D. Jatti, acting President of India (1977), died.
The new rapid-transit system established a model for modern metro rail development across Indian cities.

text: The Godhra train burning and the Gujarat riots
detail: Fifty-nine pilgrims die in the Sabarmati Express fire at Godhra on 27 February; in the violence that follows across Gujarat, more than a thousand people — most of them Muslim — are killed.
M. S. Subbulakshmi, the Carnatic vocalist who became one of India’s most celebrated classical musicians, died.
P. V. Narasimha Rao, Prime Minister of India (1991–1996), died.

text: The Indian Ocean tsunami strikes South Asia
detail: The tsunami caused catastrophic loss of life and displacement in India, Sri Lanka, the Maldives and other Indian Ocean countries.
K. R. Narayanan, President of India (1997–2002), died.

text: The Right to Information Act is enacted
detail: The law gave citizens a powerful mechanism to obtain government records and transformed transparency and accountability.

text: The rural employment guarantee law is enacted
detail: The legislation created a legal entitlement to wage employment for rural households and became one of the world’s largest social-protection programmes.
Bismillah Khan, the shehnai maestro who brought the instrument to the centre of Indian classical concert culture, died.

text: The rural employment guarantee programme begins
detail: Implementation started in two hundred districts before expanding nationwide, creating a large public-works and income-support system.
Chandra Shekhar, Prime Minister of India (1990–1991), died.
Baba Amte, the social worker who built institutions for people affected by leprosy and championed environmental and human-rights causes, died.
V. P. Singh, Prime Minister of India (1989–1990), died.

text: Chandrayaan-1 launches India’s lunar exploration programme
detail: The mission mapped the Moon and provided decisive evidence of water molecules on the lunar surface.
Ten Lashkar-e-Taiba gunmen from Karachi attack the Taj and Oberoi hotels, CST station and Nariman House over three days, killing 166 people.
R. Venkataraman, President of India (1987–1992), died.

text: The Right to Education Act is enacted
detail: The law made free and compulsory elementary education a legal right for children aged six to fourteen.

text: The Unique Identification Authority of India is established
detail: UIDAI began building Aadhaar, a nationwide biometric digital-identity system that later became central to public-service delivery and payments.

text: The first Aadhaar number is issued
detail: The biometric identity programme began enrolment at scale and later became a foundational component of India’s digital public infrastructure.
Bhimsen Joshi, the Hindustani vocalist and leading exponent of the Kirana gharana, died.
M. F. Husain, the modernist painter whose work became central to twentieth-century Indian art, died.

text: India records its last wild-polio case
detail: The absence of further cases led to India being certified polio-free in 2014, a major public-health achievement.

text: India win the Cricket World Cup at home
detail: M.S. Dhoni's six at the Wankhede seals victory over Sri Lanka — India's second World Cup, 28 years after 1983.

text: The census records India’s population above 1.2 billion
detail: The enumeration provided the demographic foundation for planning, representation, welfare and research in the new decade.
I. K. Gujral, Prime Minister of India (1997–1998), died.
Ravi Shankar, the sitarist and composer who became a global ambassador of Hindustani classical music, died.
Manna Dey, the playback singer celebrated for classical versatility and a vast multilingual film repertoire, died.

text: The Mars Orbiter Mission is launched
detail: Mangalyaan placed India on a path to become the first nation to reach Mars orbit on its maiden attempt.
Khushwant Singh, the novelist, historian, editor and public commentator whose work shaped modern Indian English prose, died.

text: India’s Mars Orbiter Mission enters orbit around Mars
detail: India became the first Asian country to reach Mars orbit and the first nation to succeed on its initial Mars mission.

text: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana launches mass financial inclusion
detail: The programme opened basic bank accounts at unprecedented scale and later supported direct benefit transfers and digital payments.
The creation of Telangana concluded a long regional movement and reorganised the political geography of the Telugu-speaking region.

text: Death: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
detail: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, the aerospace scientist and president associated with India’s missile and space programmes, died.

text: Cochin airport becomes the world’s first fully solar-powered airport
detail: A large solar plant enabled the airport to meet its electricity needs from renewable energy.
The programme coordinated broadband, digital services, electronic governance and citizen access to public platforms.

text: The International Solar Alliance is launched
detail: India and France initiated a global coalition to expand solar deployment and finance in sun-rich countries.
The withdrawal of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes caused a nationwide cash shock and accelerated formalisation and digital payments.

text: The Unified Payments Interface is launched
detail: UPI created an interoperable real-time bank-payment layer that transformed retail payments and became a core part of India’s digital public infrastructure.

text: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code is enacted
detail: The code created a time-bound framework for corporate insolvency and reshaped credit markets, creditor rights and business exit.

text: The Goods and Services Tax is introduced
detail: GST replaced numerous central and state indirect taxes with a nationwide value-added tax system and common digital compliance network.

text: The South Asia Satellite is launched
detail: India placed a communications satellite in orbit to provide services to participating South Asian countries.
Atal Bihari Vajpayee, the poet-politician and prime minister associated with coalition governance, infrastructure and nuclear policy, died.

text: Ayushman Bharat launches a national health-protection programme
detail: The initiative combined health and wellness centres with publicly financed hospital coverage for low-income families.

text: The Supreme Court decriminalises consensual same-sex relations
detail: The Navtej Singh Johar judgment struck down the colonial-era criminal prohibition and affirmed dignity, privacy and equality.
Girish Karnad, the playwright, actor and public intellectual who transformed modern Indian theatre, died.
Although its lander was lost during descent, the orbiter began a productive long-term scientific mission around the Moon.

text: Vande Bharat Express enters commercial service
detail: The indigenous semi-high-speed train introduced a new platform for intercity passenger rail design and manufacturing.

text: Article 370 is revoked; Jammu & Kashmir reorganised
detail: Parliament ends the state's special constitutional status and divides it into two union territories — Jammu & Kashmir, and Ladakh.
Irrfan Khan, the actor whose work bridged Indian independent cinema, popular film and international productions, died.
Pranab Mukherjee, President of India (2012–2017), died.
S. P. Balasubrahmanyam, the multilingual playback singer whose recordings shaped South Indian and Hindi cinema, died.

text: India enters a nationwide COVID-19 lockdown
detail: The unprecedented restrictions sought to slow the pandemic but caused major economic disruption, migration and changes in work, education and public health.

text: The National Education Policy 2020 is approved
detail: The policy proposed major changes in school structure, higher education, multidisciplinary learning, languages and regulation.
Dilip Kumar, the actor whose performances helped define naturalistic acting in Hindi cinema, died.
Milkha Singh, the sprinter whose international achievements made him an enduring icon of Indian athletics, died.

text: India administers one billion COVID-19 vaccine doses
detail: Crossing the billion-dose threshold demonstrated the scale of the country’s vaccination logistics and digital certification system.

text: India begins its nationwide COVID-19 vaccination campaign
detail: The campaign deployed domestically manufactured and imported vaccines through one of the world’s largest public-health operations.
Lata Mangeshkar, the playback singer whose voice shaped the musical memory of Indian cinema for generations, died.
The rollout began a new generation of mobile connectivity for high-speed data, industrial applications and digital services.

text: Vikram-S becomes India’s first privately built rocket to launch
detail: Skyroot Aerospace’s suborbital mission marked the entry of private Indian companies into rocket launch operations.
M. S. Swaminathan, the agricultural scientist associated with India’s Green Revolution and food-security strategy, died.

text: Aditya-L1 launches on India’s first solar mission
detail: The observatory was sent toward the Sun–Earth L1 point to study the solar corona, solar wind and space weather.

text: Chandrayaan-3 lands near the lunar south polar region
detail: India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first to land in the high southern latitudes.

text: India’s new Parliament building is inaugurated
detail: The purpose-built complex replaced the colonial-era chamber as the principal meeting place of the national legislature.

text: The women’s reservation constitutional amendment is enacted
detail: The amendment provides for one-third reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies after delimitation.
M. T. Vasudevan Nair, the writer and screenwriter who profoundly shaped modern Malayalam literature and cinema, died.
Manmohan Singh, the economist and prime minister associated with the 1991 reforms and a decade of national government, died.
Ratan Tata, the industrialist and philanthropist who led the Tata group through global expansion, died.
Shyam Benegal, the filmmaker who helped establish India’s parallel-cinema movement, died.
Zakir Hussain, the tabla virtuoso and global ambassador of Indian classical music, died.

text: Aditya-L1 enters its halo orbit around the Sun–Earth L1 point
detail: The solar observatory reached its operational orbit, enabling continuous study of the Sun and space weather.
Agnibaan SOrTeD flew from a private launchpad at Sriharikota using a single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.

text: Atal Setu opens across Mumbai Harbour
detail: The Mumbai Trans Harbour Link became India’s longest bridge and shortened travel between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai.

text: India’s first underwater metro section is inaugurated
detail: The Howrah–Esplanade metro section introduced passenger rail tunnels beneath the Hooghly River.

text: Pakistan launches its first lunar satellite mission
detail: ICUBE-Qamar travelled aboard China’s Chang’e 6 mission and became Pakistan’s first lunar and deep-space spacecraft.

text: Ram Lalla is consecrated in the new Ayodhya temple
detail: The pran pratishtha ceremony became a major religious and cultural event followed across India and the Hindu diaspora.

text: The Ahom Moidams become a UNESCO World Heritage Site
detail: The mound-burial landscape at Charaideo received recognition as a distinctive royal funerary tradition of the Ahom dynasty.

text: The new Nalanda University campus is inaugurated
detail: The Rajgir campus linked a modern international university with the intellectual heritage of ancient Nalanda.

text: India’s new criminal-law codes come into force
detail: Three statutes replaced the core colonial-era penal, criminal-procedure and evidence laws.
Dharmendra, the actor whose six-decade career made him one of Hindi cinema’s most enduring stars, died.
Jayant Narlikar, the astrophysicist, science communicator and founding director of IUCAA, died.
K. Kasturirangan, the space scientist and former ISRO chairman who also led major education-policy work, died.
Kumudini Lakhia, the dancer and choreographer who transformed modern Kathak ensemble work, died.
P. Jayachandran, the multilingual playback singer closely associated with Malayalam and Tamil cinema, died.

text: Deepavali enters UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list
detail: The inscription recognised the festival as a living tradition shared across regions, communities and the global South Asian diaspora.

text: India demonstrates satellite docking with SpaDeX
detail: ISRO docked two spacecraft in orbit, gaining a capability required for future space stations, crew transfer and in-orbit assembly.

text: Shubhanshu Shukla becomes the first Indian to visit the ISS
detail: The Axiom Mission 4 astronaut became the second Indian in space and gained experience relevant to Gaganyaan.

text: The Chenab and Anji bridges open with the Kashmir rail link
detail: The project completed an all-weather railway connection into the Kashmir Valley through difficult Himalayan terrain.

text: The Maratha Military Landscapes become a World Heritage Site
detail: UNESCO recognised a serial group of forts adapted to mountain, coastal and island terrain.
The radar mission began global observation of changes in forests, ice, groundwater, earthquakes and the Earth’s surface.

text: The new Pamban vertical-lift railway bridge opens
detail: The bridge restored the rail link to Rameswaram with a movable central span for shipping.

text: Vizhinjam deepwater transshipment port is dedicated
detail: India’s first purpose-built container transshipment port opened near major east–west shipping routes.
Asha Bhosle, the playback singer whose multilingual and stylistically diverse career spanned more than eight decades, died.
Raghu Rai, the photographer whose images documented India’s public life and the Bhopal disaster, died.
Suman Kalyanpur, the multilingual playback singer known for a long career in Hindi and regional cinema, died.

text: India approves its first dengue vaccine
detail: Regulators approved QDENGA for people aged four to sixty, creating the country’s first authorised vaccine against dengue.

text: India inaugurates its first indigenous hydrogen-powered train
detail: The ten-coach train demonstrated passenger-scale hydrogen fuel-cell propulsion on the Jind–Sonipat corridor.

text: Nuclear heat powers a thermochemical hydrogen facility
detail: The Kalpakkam project demonstrated hydrogen production using a copper–chlorine cycle and heat from the Fast Breeder Test Reactor.

text: The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor attains first criticality
detail: The 500 MWe reactor at Kalpakkam achieved a sustained controlled chain reaction, advancing the second stage of India’s nuclear programme.

text: Vikram-I completes India’s first private orbital launch
detail: Skyroot Aerospace placed payloads into orbit from Sriharikota, marking the first orbital launch by a private Indian company from Indian soil.
